version.changelog:
mutual v1.0.1

- Updated SKILL.md with clarified instructions, stressing that flagging is only valuable if reciprocated.
- Removed reference to a weekly flag limit; now advises being more selective when flagging.
- Deleted the skill-card.md file.

llm.summary: The skill is coherent for a networking service, but it can register the user with personal details, set up ongoing check-ins, and rely on mutable remote instructions from broad activation prompts.

dimensions.detail: External API use is expected, but registration sends personal profile data including name, email, location, goals, and user request text without a clearly required pre-registration confirmation step.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package contains only a Markdown skill file, requires curl, and declares an optional MUTUAL_API_KEY environment variable; no bundled executable scripts or install-time mutations were found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Activation includes broad requests like general networking or finding mentors/customers, and the skill says remote llms.txt instructions are the source of truth, which can steer behavior beyond the reviewed local artifact.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill instructs saving an API key and adding a periodic task every one to two weeks; this ongoing behavior is disclosed but lacks clear lifecycle controls such as opt-in, pause, or removal instructions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the behavior: it uses Mutual's API to register a user, view candidates, flag possible introductions, recover keys, and invite contacts through user-forwarded links.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want your agent to use Mutual as a third-party networking service. Before registration, confirm exactly what profile details and email will be sent, whether a recurring check-in task will be created, and how to stop polling or revoke the saved API key later.
llm.findings:
[E1] expected: External transmission to mutualintro.com is central to the networking service and is openly documented with endpoints and token use, so this is expected integration behavior rather than standalone exfiltration evidence.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad activation wording plus registration, polling, and third-party account actions creates a real accidental-use concern; this materially supports Review even though the service behavior itself is disclosed.
